title: Astragaloside IV Relieves Mitochondrial Oxidative Stress Damage and Dysfunction in Diabetic Mice Endothelial Progenitor Cells by Regulating the GSK-3beta/Nrf2 Axis.
authors: Zou, Xiaoling; Liu, Xiangnan; Qu, Wenjing; Zhang, Xi; Zou, Yixian; Lin, Xiangdong; Hu, Wenxiao; Gao, Ruchun; He, Youyuan; Zhou, Siyuan; Huang, Yuxuan; Xiong, Wu
one_liner_zh: 研究黄芪甲苷通过GSK-3beta/Nrf2轴缓解糖尿病小鼠内皮祖细胞线粒体氧化应激损伤，仅涉及小分子-蛋白对接，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系、结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Dysregulation of mitochondrial activity is a major cause of diabetes mellitus (DM) and its complications. Astragaloside IV, a natural herbal product, possesses protective properties against DM. This study aimed to evaluate how astragaloside IV affects oxidative stress and mitochondrial function in endothelial progenitor cells (EPCs) and elucidate the underlying mechanisms. A high glucose (HG)-induced human EPC (hEPC) model and a streptozotocin (STZ)-induced DM mouse model were established to investigate the effects of astragaloside IV on EPC function and wound healing in the context of DM. In HG-exposed hEPCs, astragaloside IV reduced apoptosis and increased cell viability and tube formation (P < 0.05). In STZ-induced DM mice, astragaloside IV promoted wound healing and increased the expression of the endothelial marker CD31 (P < 0.05) in wound tissues. In addition, the regulation of oxidative damage and mitochondrial dysfunction by astragaloside IV was investigated. We found that astragaloside IV attenuated mitochondrial damage, decreased ROS and mtROS levels (P < 0.05), decreased MDA activity and enhanced SOD activity (P < 0.05), and downregulated DPR1 levels and upregulated MFN1, MFN2, and OPA1 levels (P < 0.05). Mechanistically, the potential involvement of GSK-3beta/Nrf2 was investigated by molecular docking and intervention with the GSK-3beta activator sodium nitroprusside (SNP). Astragaloside IV was confirmed to dock with GSK-3beta, and it increased the phosphorylation of GSK-3beta (P < 0.05) and the expression of Nrf2 as well as its downstream factors HO-1 and NQO1 (P < 0.05). SNP reversed the protective effects of astragaloside IV. These results indicated that astragaloside IV attenuated HG- and STZ-induced injury through the GSK-3beta/Nrf2 pathway. These results revealed that astragaloside IV may have the potential to be an active component for protection against DM and its complications.
abstract_zh: 线粒体活性失调是糖尿病（DM）及其并发症的主要原因之一。黄芪甲苷IV作为一种天然草药产品，具有对抗糖尿病的保护特性。本研究旨在评估黄芪甲苷IV如何影响内皮祖细胞（EPCs）中的氧化应激和线粒体功能，并阐明其潜在机制。建立了高糖（HG）诱导的人内皮祖细胞（hEPC）模型和链脲佐菌素（STZ）诱导的糖尿病小鼠模型，以研究黄芪甲苷IV在糖尿病背景下对EPC功能和伤口愈合的影响。在HG暴露的hEPCs中，黄芪甲苷IV减少了细胞凋亡，并增加了细胞活力和管形成能力（P < 0.05）。在STZ诱导的糖尿病小鼠中，黄芪甲苷IV促进了伤口愈合，并增加了伤口组织中内皮标志物CD31的表达（P < 0.05）。此外，研究了黄芪甲苷IV对氧化损伤和线粒体功能障碍的调节作用。我们发现黄芪甲苷IV减轻了线粒体损伤，降低了ROS和mtROS水平（P < 0.05），降低了MDA活性并增强了SOD活性（P < 0.05），同时下调了DPR1水平并上调了MFN1、MFN2和OPA1水平（P < 0.05）。在机制上，通过分子对接和GSK-3beta激活剂硝普钠（SNP）的干预，探讨了GSK-3beta/Nrf2的潜在参与。黄芪甲苷IV被确认与GSK-3beta对接，并增加了GSK-3beta的磷酸化（P < 0.05）以及Nrf2及其下游因子HO-1和NQO1的表达（P < 0.05）。SNP逆转了黄芪甲苷IV的保护作用。这些结果表明，黄芪甲苷IV通过GSK-3beta/Nrf2通路减轻了HG和STZ诱导的损伤。这些结果揭示，黄芪甲苷IV可能具有作为对抗糖尿病及其并发症的活性成分的潜力。
